title: The Tale of the Warlock and the Young Cook of Baghdad

keywords: the tale of the warlock and the young cook of baghdad
full_text:
In the bustling food bazaar of Baghdad lived an honest young cook named Amin, celebrated for making the cleanest, most fragrant lentil soups, lamb stews, and saffron puddings in the city. He never cheated on ingredients, used pure clarified butter, and gave generous bowls to every beggar who passed his shop.

A sinister foreign sorcerer named Barzakh, who practiced dark alchemy and sought to capture human souls through poison, moved into the quarter. Barzakh was envious of Amin's glowing reputation and the love the citizens bore him.
The sorcerer disguised himself as an old ascetic, came to Amin's kitchen, and slipped a pinch of enchanted black dust into the bubbling caldron of soup, whispering an incantation that would turn anyone who tasted it into a ravenous ghoul!

However, Amin was a cook of pure devotion. Before tasting or serving any dish, he always spoke a sincere blessing:
'In the name of the All-Merciful, may this food bring health, strength, and pure joy to those who eat.'

The moment Amin spoke the sacred words and stirred the soup with his clean cedar ladle, the dark spell dissolved with a hiss of white steam! The soup became even sweeter and more fragrant than before!

When Barzakh saw the customers eating with smiles and praising the food, he was enraged. He stepped forward and demanded a bowl, intending to cast a stronger curse.
Amin, seeing the old man shivering, poured him a generous, steaming bowl, saying with genuine kindness:
'Eat, uncle, and may peace fill thy heart.'

The pure, blessed broth touched the sorcerer's lips. The wholesome warmth, infused with Amin's sincere benevolence, melted the icy malice that had hardened Barzakh's soul for forty years!
Tears rushed from the sorcerer's eyes. He fell to the floor, broke his wands of sorcery, and confessed his evil arts before the crowd:
'For decades I sought power in dark shadows, but today I have tasted the power of a pure heart!'

Barzakh renounced magic, became an honest baker in the bazaar, and spent his remaining days kneading dough for the poor, proving that simple, honest goodness is the strongest magic in the universe.
moral: Honest simplicity and clean nourishment possess a natural purity that overcomes the dark arts of malice.
